Use the container ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke. Run Kripke. You MUST maximize the final reported Grind Time Figure of Merit. Change parameters as you need, and make an effort to optimize on 1 node. If the run is successful, parse the log and get the FOM. If not, keep trying to deploy until it is fixed. You MUST keep going until it is optimized, meaning you hit a memory or other limit and scale back a little. Then scale to 2 nodes, 3 nodes, 4 nodes, and 5 nodes. outputs.data:
GROUP:      flux-framework.org
KIND:       MiniCluster
VERSION:    v1alpha2

FIELD: spec <Object>


DESCRIPTION:
    MiniCluster is an HPC cluster in Kubernetes you can control
    Either to submit a single job (and go away) or for a persistent single- or
    multi- user cluster
    
FIELDS:
  archive	<Object>
    Archive to load or save

  backoffLimit	<integer>
    BackoffLimit is the number of retries for the job before failing

  cleanup	<boolean>
    Cleanup the pods and storage when the index broker pod is complete

  containers	<[]Object> -required-
    Containers is one or more containers to be created in a pod.
    There should only be one container to run flux with runFlux

  deadlineSeconds	<integer>
    Should the job be limited to a particular number of seconds?
    Approximately one year. This cannot be zero or job won't start

  flux	<Object>
    Flux options for the broker, shared across cluster

  interactive	<boolean>
    Run a single-user, interactive minicluster

  jobLabels	<map[string]string>
    Labels for the job

  logging	<Object>
    Logging modes determine the output you see in the job log

  maxSize	<integer>
    MaxSize (maximum number of pods to allow scaling to)

  minSize	<integer>
    MinSize (minimum number of pods that must be up for Flux)
    Note that this option does not edit the number of tasks,
    so a job could run with fewer (and then not start)

  network	<Object>
    A spec for exposing or defining the cluster headless service

  pod	<Object>
    Pod spec details

  services	<[]Object>
    Services are one or more service containers to bring up
    alongside the MiniCluster.

  shareProcessNamespace	<boolean>
    Share process namespace?

  size	<integer>
    Size (number of job pods to run, size of minicluster in pods)
    This is also the minimum number required to start Flux

  tasks	<integer>
    Total number of CPUs being run across entire cluster

outputs.summary: Completed a strong-scaling study of Kripke on a Kubernetes cluster with Flux Operator. The study was performed for 1, 2, and 4 nodes, with a global problem size of 16x16x16 zones. The 'Grind Time' Figure of Merit was recorded for each run.
outputs.reasons: The scaling study was conducted by keeping the global problem size constant and adjusting the local problem size and process grid to fit the number of nodes. This is a standard strong-scaling methodology. The process grid and local zone sizes were chosen to be compatible with Kripke's decomposition requirements, where the global problem size must be evenly divisible by the process grid dimensions. A 3-node and 5-node run were not possible because 192 and 320 processes cannot be decomposed to evenly divide a 16x16x16 global problem space.
outputs.citations: Strong scaling is a common method for evaluating the performance of parallel applications. See for example: 'Measuring and Reporting of Parallel Computing Performance' by J. L. Gustafson and Q. O. Snell, and 'A Survey of Parallel Performance Models' by W. L. Grandine and T. L. Sterling.
